answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. The practical upshot is that honesty is the only strategy that scales — a farm that tries to game the system pays for each identity it adds. Consider a trellis as the anchor of the cost. A garden stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a walnut holds the reputation...
